Project steering is guidance that belongs to one repository or work area: build commands, architecture, coding standards, deployment facts, and local conventions.

## Current behavior

Consuelo OS does **not** automatically merge arbitrary project files into `get_steering`. The OS bootstrap loads the workspace files under `~/.consuelo/steering`.

Project-aware agents should then read the instruction files in the repository they are working in. Common names include:

```text
AGENTS.md
CODING-STANDARDS.md
README.md
<package>/AGENTS.md
```

Use the project's actual convention rather than assuming every repository has all of these files.

## What belongs in project guidance

Good project guidance covers facts that are true for that codebase:

- package boundaries and ownership;
- required tests and build commands;
- architecture and deployment constraints;
- formatting and naming conventions;
- known runtime gotchas;
- where task-specific records live.

Temporary acceptance criteria and progress belong in the task's workpad, not in permanent steering.

## Precedence

System and workspace policy remain in force. Project instructions can narrow how work is performed inside that project, but they cannot loosen an OS permission, security rule, or approval boundary.

When instructions disagree, stop and resolve the conflict rather than choosing the most convenient file.
